stories.title: Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle, CB Riley Moss suffer concussions against Panthers
stories.summary: Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss both suffered concussions against the Panthers.
stories.detail: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss sustained concussions within minutes of each other in Denver's 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The Broncos went into the game without either of their starting safeties as Brandon Jones (hamstring) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both game-day inactives. Second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron played in Moss' spot. Moss was injured as he made a tackle on Trevor Etienne in the second quarter. Waddle, who had one catch Sunday for 22 yards, left the game with seconds to go in the first quarter. He reached to make a catch in front of Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson and was hit by Zakee Wheatley , who knocked the ball free. Waddle, who has battled ankle and chest injuries already this season, jumped up after the play and walked toward the Broncos huddle but then left the field and did not return. He has 30 receptions for 337 yards and two touchdowns this season. The Broncos (6-2) entered the day with a slim lead in the AFC West race over the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2).

stories.detail: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — Patrick Mahomes threw for 242 yards with a pair of touchdown passes to Kenneth Walker, who added 102 yards and a score on the ground, and the Kansas City Chiefs got back on track with a 35-12 rout of the hapless New York Jets on Sunday. Walker finished with 143 yards from scrimmage and the Chiefs sacked Geno Smith five times while keeping the Jets out of the end zone, allowing Kansas City (6-2) to erase the stink of consecutive losses to the Seahawks and Broncos. Smith finished with 165 yards passing for the Jets (2-7), who lost their fourth straight. They were credited with minus-9 yards of offense in the third quarter, when Kansas City scored a pair of touchdowns that turned a 14-12 halftime lead into a comfortable victory. The Chiefs have beaten New York in each of their last three meetings. The Jets, missing star wide receiver Garrett Wilson to a concussion , were reduced to running the ball with Braelon Allen or Breece Hall — back from a quadriceps injury for the first time in five games — or having Smith throw short passes to rookie Omar Cooper Jr . stories.title: Thunder get Nique Clifford in trade with Kings
stories.summary: The Thunder have acquired 2025 first-round pick Nique Clifford in a trade with the Kings.
stories.detail: The Kings have traded second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Thunder for two second-round picks, Oklahoma City announced Sunday. In return, the Kings will receive a 2028 Utah Jazz second-rounder and a 2030 Minnesota Timberwolves second-rounder out of the Thunder's deep asset cupboard. The Kings initially acquired Clifford in the 2025 draft, trading a top-16-protected 2027 San Antonio Spurs first-round pick to the Thunder to move up to the No. 24 pick and grab Clifford. It was the first move of general manager Scott Perry's tenure. But Clifford never caught on in Sacramento and has recently been buried in coach Doug Christie's rotation despite injuries ahead of him, leading both sides -- the Kings' and Clifford's -- to seek a new home for the 24-year-old. The Thunder are in need on the wing after a rash of early-season injuries. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace , both starters, are out for several months and perhaps the entire season. Wallace tore the labrum in his left shoulder and Williams fractured his left fibula and dislocated his left ankle in the same late October home game against the LA Clippers . stories.detail: Second-year wing Nique Clifford was not getting much run in Sacramento, he was unimpressive in Summer League, but the real question has been: Is that because Clifford is not really an NBA player, or is it because of the Kings and coach Doug Christie's player development and usage? The Oklahoma City Thunder are betting on the latter, as they have agreed to trade for Clifford from the Kings for two second-round picks (Utah's 2028 and Minnesota's 2030), a story broken by Shams Charania of ESPN . The Thunder are looking for wing depth after potential season-ending injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Clifford, the No. 24 pick in 2025 out of Colorado State, had largely fallen out of the Kings' rotation, and the team worked with him to find a new home, Charania reports. Clifford will make $3.3 million this season and $3.4 million next season, with a team option for nearly $6 million for 2028-29. Clifford, a 6'5" wing, was averaging 6.3 minutes per game for the Kings, averaging 1.6 points per game on 35.3% shooting. stories.title: Is Luka Dončić playing tonight? Injury update on Lakers star vs. Pistons
stories.summary: The Lakers will be without the driving force of their offense against one of the best defenses in the NBA to start their four-game road trip.
stories.detail: The Los Angeles Lakers are tasked with facing one of the NBA's best defenses in the Detroit Pistons in the first of their four-game road trip on Sunday, Nov. 8. They'll have the added challenge of doing so without the driving force of their offense. Luka Dončić has been ruled out with lower back tightness, the team announced. Dončić was listed as questionable on Saturday, one day after the leading MVP candidate dropped a season-high 53 points at home against the Portland Trail Blazers . It's a blow to the Lakers (8-2), who will be without Dončić's 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists per night in nine games played this season. He's missed one other game with back tightness. Detroit (6-2), meanwhile, has given up an average of 101.8 points per game, fewest in the league. Amid Dončić's historic stretch of seven consecutive 35-plus point games, the last four of which he's scored at least 40, head coach JJ Redick was asked if there was any danger in relying too much on the two-time scoring champion. You’re in the back seat of your mom’s car, those sweet sweet Golden Arches come into view, and you make your pitch: “Mom, can we PLEAAASEEE get McDonald’s?” And without missing a beat, back comes the dreamcrushing sentence masquerading as a better suggestion: “We got McDonald’s at home.” What’s at home is never McDonald’s, but it’s ground beef, sandwich bread, ketchup, mustard, and relish. You eat it and more often than not depending on who your mama is, it hits. Your tastebuds are awash with flavor and gratitude. Maybe mom was right,…
